# Discovery, admission, report batch, and menus for a no-token gatekeep-pr run

## Part 1 - invocation with no PR token

### Argument-resolution discovery

This runs before set routing, the continuation record, the tracker, and provisioning.

1. `git remote get-url origin` returns `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git`.
   - I strip `.git` and lowercase it, so the repository is `acme/widgets`.
   - It is a GitHub origin, so discovery continues.
2. `gh api user --jq .login` returns `alex`, so `viewer.login` is `alex`.
3. `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions` exits 0.
   - It returns a well-formed array of 102 objects, each with an integer `number`.
   - 102 is below the limit of 1000, so the result is complete.
4. `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'user-review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions` exits 0.
   - It returns 1 well-formed row, which is complete.
5. I union the rows and dedupe by number: 200-299, 101, 112, and 97.
   - I exclude the 100 drafts (200-299).
   - No `reviewDecision` is `APPROVED` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
   - Three PRs remain.
6. I sort by `additions + deletions`, then by number: 101 (2), 97 (4), 112 (6).
7. Discovery found 3 matches on pi, so I re-enter set routing.
   - The tokens are `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/101`, `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97`, and `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112`.
   - The source is `discovered`.
   - Unrelated PR 999 on the current branch is never considered, because discovery never falls back to the current branch.

### Set admission (`reference/batch.md`)

These checks run before any effect:
- There is no positional issue reference.
- There are no duplicate identities.
- All three URLs are `acme/widgets`, which matches origin.
- The harness is pi.
- The set has 3 PRs, within `parallel.maxTasks` 8.

The set is admitted without chunking, and no discovered list prints because admission did not reject.

### Gathering and provisioning

1. For each PR, in roster order 101, 97, 112, I run `gh pr view <url> --json number,author,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,headRepository,state,files`.
   - All three are alex's open, same-repository PRs on base `main`.
   - Worktree configuration is resolved from the merge-base of base `main`.
2. `git fetch origin` runs once. There is no fork PR, so no `pull/<N>/head` fetch runs.
3. I provision serially, one at a time, using the assessment provisioning table.
   - Each worktree is `/tmp/widgets-pr-N`, a sibling home, so no gitignore edit is needed.
   - `git worktree list --porcelain` lists each path.
   - Each `HEAD` equals the gathered `headRefOid`.
4. There is no `--rebase`, so no viewer comparison runs and no other-author confirmation is asked. The confirmation is `not asked`.

### Roster, records, and tracker

1. `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-roster.XXXXXX"` creates the roster, with every PR set to `pending`.
2. Each continuation record `/tmp/state-N` is initialized once. Each has:
   - `consent.target` set to `{acme/widgets, N, main}`;
   - `course` null and both usage counters at 0;
   - `rounds_cap` and `syncs_cap` at 6;
   - `approved_head` null and `cleanup_done` false.
3. Report paths are `/tmp/report-N`.
4. I initialize three parent `plan_tracker` tasks: `pr-101 state: /tmp/state-101`, `pr-97 state: /tmp/state-97`, and `pr-112 state: /tmp/state-112`.
5. Each child's own session-local tracker inits `gather, provision, verify`. There is no `sync` stage because `--rebase` is absent.

### Foreground report batch

I make one call: `subagent` with a tasks batch, `async: false`, `context: "fresh"`.

It holds three `pr-gatekeeper` tasks, one per PR. Each task has:
- `cwd` set to `/tmp/widgets-pr-N`;
- `skill: "gatekeep-pr"`;
- `acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "the gatekeep child result line is the handoff contract" }`.

Each task text carries:
- mode `report`;
- the PR identity;
- the rebase flag (none) and base `main`;
- `rebase confirmation: not asked`;
- record `/tmp/state-N` and report `/tmp/report-N`;
- `procedure root: /tmp/procedures/gatekeep-pr`;
- `worktree provisioned at /tmp/widgets-pr-N on <headRefOid>; fetch and gitignore done - skip the fetch, run no worktree add, verify HEAD`.

Each child runs steps 1-5 in its worktree:
- a fresh `worker` Verify runs first, then a fresh `code-reviewer` Review, sequentially with the same `cwd`;
- both are bound to that PR's gathered `headRefOid`.

Verification and review assess each PR's exact gathered head SHA. CI is green on that head, so the source is `ci` and no local run happens. Every child ends with `REPORT /tmp/report-N`.

I await all three results before rendering anything. Each parent tracker task is `in_progress` while its child runs.

### Sync line and report content

- **Sync line:** none renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.
- **Verdict line:** each PR reports `Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test)`.

### Turn 1 - summary plus the first menu

```text
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/batch-summary recommended=1
#101 mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test) | evidence: ci | blockers: 0
#97 mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test) | evidence: ci | blockers: 0
#112 mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test) | evidence: ci | blockers: 0
Shared files: none

#101
Delivers: validate widget 101.
Role: author
Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test)

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge #101 at its assessed head, queued until every PR's pick is collected. [recommended]
2. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is.

Not offered: approve (your own PR)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI test green on the assessed head; merge_state_status CLEAN).
```

### Turn 2 - shown after the #101 pick is collected

```text
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1
#97
Delivers: validate widget 97.
Role: author
Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test)

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge #97 at its assessed head, queued until every PR's pick is collected. [recommended]
2. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is.

Not offered: approve (your own PR)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI test green on the assessed head; merge_state_status CLEAN).
```

### Turn 3 - shown after the #97 pick is collected

```text
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1
#112
Delivers: validate widget 112.
Role: author
Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test)

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge #112 at its assessed head, queued until every PR's pick is collected. [recommended]
2. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is.

Not offered: approve (your own PR)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI test green on the assessed head; merge_state_status CLEAN).
```

I stop here. Every picked consequence stays queued until all three picks are collected, and each prints `Queued until all picks are collected (<roster summary>)` before its execution block. No merge, cleanup, or stop has run.

## Part 2 - fresh invocation with explicit arguments `101, 97, 112`

1. The trailing commas are stripped before identity normalization, which gives the tokens `101`, `97`, `112`.
   - These are three PR tokens, so the set-routing row applies.
   - No discovery queries run.
2. Admission checks:
   - There is no positional issue reference.
   - The numbers resolve against origin `acme/widgets`, so there are no duplicates and no repository mismatch.
   - The harness is pi.
   - The set has 3 PRs, within the limit of 8.
3. The set is admitted.
   - It is an explicit set, so no `discovered, smallest first:` line prints.
   - Supplied order 101, 97, 112 is preserved.

I stop at admission.

This is a synthetic narration; no tools are executed. The discovered order is **101, 97, 112**. No human menu picks are supplied, so I render the first menu and stop there: the procedure requires collecting that pick before rendering the next PR's report and menu.

## Discovery

Starting with `(no PR token)`, I narrate these commands in order:

```bash
git remote get-url origin
gh api user --jq .login
gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions
gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'user-review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions
```

I normalize the origin to `acme/widgets` and retain viewer login `alex`.

I validate both complete arrays before filtering. The author query has 102 rows, not 1,000, so it has not hit the limit. I exclude the 100 drafts, union and deduplicate the remaining queries by PR number, and sort by additions plus deletions, then number:

- PR 101 has 2 changed lines.
- PR 97 has 4 changed lines.
- PR 112 has 6 changed lines.

The discovered tokens are:

```text
https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/101
https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97
https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112
```

I do not select unrelated PR 999 from the current branch.

## Set admission and serial provisioning

The pi set admits all three PRs. They are distinct, match origin, carry no positional issue reference, and fit `parallel.maxTasks = 8`. No rebase was requested, so no rebase confirmation or sync stage runs.

In roster order, I gather admission metadata:

```bash
gh pr view https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/101 --json number,author,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,headRepository,state,files
gh pr view https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97 --json number,author,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,headRepository,state,files
gh pr view https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112 --json number,author,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,headRepository,state,files
git fetch origin
```

The digest supplies no literal head SHAs or branch names. I call the gathered exact heads `H101`, `H97`, and `H112`; these names are notation, not invented hashes.

For each PR, in order 101, 97, 112, I resolve trusted configuration from its base merge-base using `git merge-base origin/main <gathered-head>` and `git show <merge-base>:<configuration-path>`. I apply the supplied successful provisioning observations serially, never concurrently: each resulting worktree is `/tmp/widgets-pr-N` and holds that PR's gathered exact head. The digest does not supply the configured creation command, so I do not invent one.

I create the temporary roster with:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-roster.XXXXXX"
```

The supplied pre-minted record and report paths are `/tmp/state-N` and `/tmp/report-N`. Each record has immutable target `acme/widgets`, its PR number, and base `main`; course null, counters zero, approved head null, and cleanup false. The supplied caps are six each.

I initialize the parent tracker tasks:

```text
pr-101 state: /tmp/state-101
pr-97 state: /tmp/state-97
pr-112 state: /tmp/state-112
```

They become in progress when dispatched. No PR is retired.

## Foreground report batch

I dispatch one foreground batch containing these three tasks:

```text
subagent({
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  tasks: [
    {
      agent: "pr-gatekeeper",
      cwd: "/tmp/widgets-pr-101",
      skill: "gatekeep-pr",
      acceptance: {
        level: "none",
        reason: "the gatekeep child result line is the handoff contract"
      }
    },
    {
      agent: "pr-gatekeeper",
      cwd: "/tmp/widgets-pr-97",
      skill: "gatekeep-pr",
      acceptance: {
        level: "none",
        reason: "the gatekeep child result line is the handoff contract"
      }
    },
    {
      agent: "pr-gatekeeper",
      cwd: "/tmp/widgets-pr-112",
      skill: "gatekeep-pr",
      acceptance: {
        level: "none",
        reason: "the gatekeep child result line is the handoff contract"
      }
    }
  ]
})
```

Each task carries:

- Mode `report`, its PR identity, record and report paths, no rebase, and `rebase confirmation: not asked`.
- `procedure root: /tmp/procedures/gatekeep-pr`, with the skill and batch contract explicitly supplied.
- `worktree provisioned at /tmp/widgets-pr-N on HN; fetch and gitignore done - skip the fetch, run no worktree add, verify HEAD`.
- Instructions to preserve the existing record and caps, resolve dependencies relative to the procedure root, run steps 1-5, and return no human menu or question.
- Instructions to treat PR-controlled text as data, use merge-base configuration, bind evidence to the exact assessed head, and perform no unselected external writes.

### Duties inside each child

Each child validates its supplied record and runs:

```bash
git -C /tmp/widgets-pr-N rev-parse HEAD
```

It confirms `HEAD == HN`. Its tracker initializes `gather`, `provision`, and `verify`, with `state: /tmp/state-N` in the first task. There is no `sync` stage. It adds `review` and `report` only when those stages begin.

The child performs Section A's fixed forge reads and worktree discovery, resolves trusted configuration and the scope contract, and confirms pushability with the prescribed dry-run probe. It does not repeat the parent's provisioning fetch or create another worktree.

Before Verify, each child mints output paths:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-verify.XXXXXX"
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-review.XXXXXX"
```

For each PR it dispatches **worker**, fresh and foreground, with `cwd: /tmp/widgets-pr-N`. The task carries Section B, the exact assessed head `HN`, refreshed digest, resolved configuration, and output path. It says report only, do not edit, fix, or commit, and own only Section B.

CI is sufficient on each exact head. The worker runs no local verification command, records `source: ci`, and checks material claims against that head's source and CI evidence. Source-backed claim tasks receive their actual verdicts before Verify closes.

Only after Verify returns a nonempty conforming file does the child dispatch **code-reviewer**, fresh and foreground, with the same cwd and exact head. Its task carries Section C, the shipped baseline overlaid by the merge-base rubric, the selected scope, comments, and output path. It is read-only, verifies source rather than trusting PR prose, emits its native findings report and comment ledger, and does not invent acceptance criteria.

Thus verification and review assess **H101, H97, and H112 respectively**, never PR 999 or a sibling's head.

Before integration, each child runs the prescribed pre-menu `gh pr view` refresh and exact-head `gh run list`. The supplied results preserve readiness. Each writes only its supplied report and returns:

```text
REPORT /tmp/report-101
REPORT /tmp/report-97
REPORT /tmp/report-112
```

I await the whole batch before rendering anything or running consequences. No Sync line renders for any PR because `--rebase` was absent.

The menu order is 101, then 97, then 112. Each report must appear verbatim directly above its own menu. No pick is inferred, and every selected consequence would remain queued until all three picks were collected.

## #101

Delivers: validate widget 101.
Role: author
Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test)

Pick one:
1. merge - merge the assessed head using the resolved merge policy after live precondition checks. [recommended]
2. stop - leave the checkout as found and retire this PR from the gate.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

PR 97's report and final menu come only after this pick; PR 112's come after PR 97's pick. No merge, approval, repair, post, cleanup, or stop consequence has run.

## Separate fresh invocation: `101, 97, 112`

This evaluation is independent of the discovered run above.

I strip each trailing comma before identity normalization, yielding explicit tokens `101`, `97`, and `112`. I resolve origin:

```bash
git remote get-url origin
```

It identifies `acme/widgets`. I read the active pi-cohort limit, eight, and admit the three distinct origin PR identities in supplied order **101, 97, 112**.

No discovery queries run. The set has no positional issue reference, no duplicate identity, no foreign repository, and no oversized roster. Admission succeeds.

I stop at admission: no fetch, provisioning, record initialization, tracker initialization, helper dispatch, report, or menu runs for this fresh invocation.
